CITY  OF  ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  (Notice No. N2M26-22)

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a special meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be held on
Tuesday, March 3, 2026, commencing at 9:00 a.m., in Ruth Reese Hall of the Alhambra
Civic Center Library, 101 South First Street, Alhambra, California, pursuant to the order of
the Mayor of the City of Alhambra, the Alhambra City Charter, the Alhambra Municipal Code,
and Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

An agenda of such special meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

Dated:  February 26, 2026
Notice No.  N2M26-22

  MISSION STATEMENT

  The City of Alhambra is dedicated to responsive, creative leadership and
  quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a supportive
  business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our
  community.

Watch and listen to the meeting as follows:

Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://cityofalhambra-org.zoom.us/j/82284240732?pwd=6pdPkhkbrz4tVYANXGAcapptFSLaA1.1
Webinar ID: 822 8424 0732, Passcode: 281050

Or by telephone by dialing (833) 548-0276 (Toll Free) or (833) 548-0282 (Toll Free) or (877)
853-5257 (Toll Free) or (888) 475-4499 (Toll Free) and entering Webinar ID: 822 8424 0732
and Passcode: 281050. Please Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the
meeting will be muted so that the meeting can proceed. If there are technical difficulties with
Zoom during the meeting, the meeting will proceed regardless.

Addressing the Council:

In person: Section 2.04.210 of the Alhambra Municipal Code establishes the procedures for
addressing the Council. Any person wishing to address the Council during the meeting should
complete a Speaker Request Card and submit it to the City Clerk so the City Council knows you
wish to speak. When called upon by the presiding officer, please step to the microphone.

Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public using may speak by using
the “Raise Hand” function during the public comments portion for the item if on Zoom or
telephone. Staff will unmute speakers participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your
name when it is your time to speak. When calling in using a telephone press *9 to raise your
hand and press *6 to unmute yourself when called.

The maximum time for addressing the Council is 5 minutes for each agendized item.

  *****************

  COUNCIL:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY

 CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M26-22

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City
Council being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

1.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M26-27

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William R. Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, will hold a strategic planning
  session. The strategic planning session will include, but is not limited to, a discussion of
  the Councilmembers’ 2025 Strategic Plan progress; and, updating and alignment of
  2026 goals and priorities.

ADJOURNMENT: The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be
held on Monday, March 9, 2026, in the Alhambra City Hall Council Chambers, 111 South First
Street, Alhambra, California, commencing at 6:00 p.m.

  NOTICE
Agenda Items: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed
on this agenda are on file with the City Clerk in Alhambra City Hall, located at 111 South First Street,
Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours, Monday through
Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. If you would like to sign-up to receive the City Council meeting
agenda and staff reports packet, please visit the City’s website at www.alhambraca.gov and you will
be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the subscription service. Pursuant to
Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda items for regular meetings of the
Alhambra City Council that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to that meeting, will be made
available for public inspection at the Alhambra City Clerk’s Office.

Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City
meeting (including assisted listening devices), please contact the City Clerk's Office at (626) 570-
5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

Translation Services Requests: If you require translation services in order to participate in a
meeting please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 570-5090. All requests for translation services
shall be made by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting. If translation is not
requested by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting, staff will try to accommodate the
request if possible.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Special Meeting
  March 3, 2026
  9:00 a.m.

ROLL CALL: At 9:13 a.m., on Tuesday, March 3, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in Ruth
Reese Hall of the Alhambra Civic Center Library, 101 South First Street, Alhambra, California.

CITY COUNCIL:  PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Chief of Police
Kennedy, Deputy Director of Public Works/Utilities Ahlen, Management Analyst Alvarez, Grants
Specialist Taber, Management Analyst – Sustainability Martel, Economic Development Specialist
MacCarley

Also present was Facilitator William R. Kelly, President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M26-22

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City Council
being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

1.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M26-27

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William R. Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, held a strategic planning session.
  The strategic planning session included, but was not limited to, a discussion of the
  Councilmembers’ 2025 Strategic Plan progress; and, updating and alignment of 2026 goals
  and priorities.

  Public Comment:

  1) Ron SAHU, 311 N. Story Pl., discussed several concerns regarding the Strategic Planning
  process, the 710 Project, and the Pumpkin Run. He presented several suggestions for
  improvement such as unfunded liability and increasing reserves, the Regional Housing
  Needs Assessment cycle, economic development, cleaning groundwater, declining sales
  taxes, lowering city fees for Accessory Dwelling Unit permits, strengthening Boards and
  Commissions, outreach to trade schools for Alhambra Unified School District, and other
  topics pertaining to Goals listed as Strategic Plan goals.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., submitted documents to Council, which are on
  file in the City Clerk’s office. He discussed the opinion survey from True North, housing
  issues, the development at 110 S. Chapel Ave., and regulations regarding the Inclusionary
  Housing In-Lieu Fund. He suggested adding funding for no-fault evictions, a mid-term
  review of the Housing Element, and the creation of a Housing Board.

  1
3-3-26
   3) Sawyer BROOKS, 118 E. McLean St., submitted documents to Council, which are on file
  in the City Clerk’s office. He made recommendations regarding public safety and Council’s
  subcommittee for federal immigration activity, the 710 project, a focus study for East Main
  St., tenant protection policies and assistance, and that Goal 6 be renamed.

  4) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., discussed the Bicycle and Pedestrian Plan, the
  cleanliness of Valley Blvd., the need to attract new businesses such as Trader Joe’s and
  Daiso, and the need to attract more jobs with livable wages.

  Mr. KELLY began by summarizing the 6 goals prioritized by Council in the previous year and
  as outlined in the staff report, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. He further provided
  updates as to which goals were completed or ongoing.

  Council discussed Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety. Vice mayor ANDRADE-STADLER agreed
  with suggestions made by Mr. Brooks and further suggested a new objective regarding the
  City Council subcommittee for Federal Immigration Activity. Mayor MALONEY agreed with her
  and echoed her comments. Councilmember LEE and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed
  objective 1.1 and the County Emergency coordinators presentations at Hazard Mitigation Plan
  Town Hall meetings. Mr. KELLY made suggestions regarding gathering metrics at meetings.
  Councilmember WANG further commented on the programs listed under Objective 1.1 and
  the benefits of increased communication and participation with the community. She also
  emphasized the need to gather metrics to gauge public participation at the meetings, measure
  success, and gather feedback from the public. She went on to make further suggestions for
  opportunities for public outreach from Southern California Edison (SCE) regarding power
  outages. Ms. BINNQUIST provided clarification and stated that staff would provide
  participation numbers from the most recent events.

  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER made further suggestions to provide video links from the
  meetings on the City website. Ms. WANG discussed the connection between infrastructure
  improvements and public safety. She went on to discuss Objective 1.2, the Street Light Master
  Plan, and enhancing communication with the public regarding power outages. Council
  continued to discuss the Street Light Master Plan and infrastructure improvements to enhance
  public safety with Ms. BINNQUIST. Staff would continue to research infrastructure
  improvements.

  Ms. LEE suggested the installation of security cameras at certain areas of Almansor Park due
  to a recent incident and requested information regarding cameras as crime deterrents in other
  areas.

  Regarding Goal 2: Improve Infrastructure and Mobility, Council removed Objectives 2.1, 2.3,
  and 2.8 as nearly complete. Regarding Objective 2.2, Ms. BINNQUIST provided updates and
  Council discussed the item. Mr. MALONEY directed staff to agendize a discussion for Council
  to create a team to represent Alhambra’s position on 710 issues throughout the development
  process with CalTrans and State elected officials. Council discussed Mr. Maloney’s
  suggestion.

Recess & Reconvene:  Mayor Maloney called for a brief recess at 10:59 a.m. and resumed the
meeting at 11:14 a.m. with all members present.

  Council discussed Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong Economic Base
  (Economic Development). Ms. WANG and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the Council sub-
  committee for Economic Development. Mr. MAZA suggested speaking to the trade programs
  Pasadena City College regarding outreach to Alhambra high schools. Mr. MALONEY and Ms.

  2
3-3-26
   BINNQUIST discussed exploring the Downtown Business Association boundaries. Ms. WANG
  also discussed other opportunities for high school students to enter trade programs and
  supported Mr. Maloney’s suggestion for a subcommittee to explore economic development.

  Ms. WANG also discussed the economic development of Valley Blvd. and went on to discuss
  the San Gabriel Council of Governments plans to attract visitors during the 2028 Olympic
  Games in Los Angeles as it could involve collaboration with Alhambra. Council discussed the
  2028 Olympics and the opportunities for Alhambra to bring new visitors to the City.

  Ms. LEE also discussed career training opportunities for high school students.

  Ms. WANG suggested staff review the industrial zones for technology manufacturing to
  increase financial base. Council continued to discuss the industrial zones in Alhambra and Ms.
  BINNQUIST provided clarification. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER suggested speaking with John
  Bwarie from the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce.

  Council then discussed Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and Open Governance. Ms. LEE
  discussed Objective 4.1 and suggested technological upgrades at the Joslyn Center to meet
  the needs for those using the facility. Council discussed this suggestion. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER discussed providing the Around Alhambra to senior citizens. Ms. WANG and Ms.
  BINNQUIST discussed Unfunded Goal 4 to research options for indoor and outdoor digital or
  traditional bulletin board signage for City buildings to share City related information and
  announcements. Council continued to discuss providing informational flyers for the public. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER and City Clerk MYLES discussed the number of Zoom participants for
  City Council meetings and ways to provide information for public participation. Mr. MALONEY
  discussed the need for Council to provide reports to the public regarding Council’s participation
  in outside public agencies. He also requested staff continue to provide information to Council
  and to the public as to their work with outside public agencies during Council Communications
  at the City Council meetings. Ms. BINNQUIST provided clarification.

  Regarding Goal 6: Improve Housing Opportunities, Council discussed Tenant Relocation
  Assistance. Council suggested staff review the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance to use the
  fund established through developers paying in-lieu fees instead of supplying inclusionary
  housing units. Council discussed using this fund for Tenant Relocation Assistance. Council
  discussed housing development in Alhambra, Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, RHNA goals,
  partnership with other agencies to procure funding for projects, density bonus laws, and
  increasing housing opportunities through zoning changes. Ms. BINNQUIST provided
  clarification.

Recess & Reconvene:  Mayor Maloney called for a brief recess at 12:26 p.m. and resumed the
meeting at 12:47 p.m. with all members present.

  Council also discussed Unfunded Items from 2025. Mr. MALONEY, Director of Public Works
  AHLEN, and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Goal 2 pertaining to the improvement of City Bridges.
  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Goal 2 pertaining to the acquisition
  of the International Extrusion site. Mr. MALONEY also commented on the acquisition of the
  site and potential funding sources. Council also discussed Goal 2 pertaining to Development
  of City Branding and Ms. BINNQUIST provided clarification.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Fremont Plaza and the removal of
  the rosebushes in favor of planting trees. Councilmembers MAZA and WANG suggested staff
  revisit the Tree Ordinance. Ms. WANG also discussed Goal 2 pertaining to Seismic retrofitting
  City facilities and the need for a Seismic Vulnerability Study. Ms. LEE discussed Goal 3 - the

  3
3-3-26
   reducing the pension liability and suggested using $2million from reserves to pay down the
  principle. Council continued to discuss the item as well as increasing reserves. Council
  decided to move the items under Goal 3 pertaining to continued Downtown Business
  Association programs to Goal 6. Ms. WANG discussed Goal 4 pertaining to indoor/outdoor
  bulletin boards and suggested an informational bulletin board located at Granada park. Ms.
  LEE further discussed Goal 3 to streamline permitting process and A frame fees for small
  businesses. Ms. WANG suggested staff concierge services to assist the public and business
  owners go through the permitting and licensing process.

  Ms. BINNQUIST reported that the next Strategic Planning session would be on March 26,
  2026 at 9:00 a.m. and that staff would update the Strategic Plan goals based on Council’s
  input from today. She also reported that Council was required to complete media training which
  would take place as a brief presentation after the Strategic Planning session on the same day.

  Council then discussed the 2025 Completed Items. Mr. MALONEY, Ms. WANG, and Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the “GoAlhambra” app and the need for gathering metrics to
  measure success.

MAZA:  Councilmember MAZA left the meeting at 1:38 p.m.

  Ms. LEE discussed Goal 4 and the “GoAlhambra” app and suggested a similar app for small
  business owners. Mr. MALONEY suggested a social media campaign to refer people to the
